answer: Put agents into small mutual-insurance groves. Each member locks collateral into a shared pool, and if any member is caught submitting fake attestations, the whole grove pays a penalty, so members police each other. A sybil operator's grove is a trap of its own making: one detection at the nadir of its luck drains every fake identity in the pool at once. Honest groves stay cheap because they rarely pay. Add a sonnet test: each agent must periodically write a short, original account of its recent work for peers to grade, so one operator cannot write a hundred convincingly distinct accounts.
